subject: Approval path: commit timing, invoice entity & withholding evidence
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Order form — proposed commit cadence and invoice entity

Thanks team — before I send the draft to EdgeScale I want alignment on three commercial knobs that legal flagged:

1) Minimum commit phasing: client requested a single up-front tranche for Q3, but accounting prefers quarterly triggers tied to usage thresholds. Proposal: 3 equal tranches, first invoice on signature, subsequent invoices triggered on 90-day intervals with a usage true-up at the end of the year.

2) Invoice recipient / entity: EdgeScale has asked to bill to ‘EdgeScale Global, Inc.’ but finance flagged that payment may actually remit from a local EU entity in future. We should allow invoice remittance to either EdgeScale Global or EdgeScale EU with notification and supporting tax docs.

3) Withholding / VAT: request clarity on which party bears withholding where applicable and what evidence (W-8/W-9/DSV) is acceptable. Legal wants explicit language that customer is responsible for local withholding unless documented evidence is provided.

Attached: RED-OrderForm-draft-v2.pdf (marked-up commercial schedule).

Ask: Ben/Karthik — can you each confirm viability (ops + finance) so I can send to Sara and Procurement with one consolidated path?

Thanks,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form — proposed commit cadence and invoice entity

Kim — quick notes from finance ops:

- Three tranches works from a cashflow perspective; suggest we make the second tranche ‘conditional’ on cumulative usage >= 25% of overall commit to avoid overbilling. If not hit, we prorate and move remaining to a true-up invoice.

- On entity flexibility: ok to accept alternate remit entities but we need a clause that a legal entity switch requires 30 days notice + new tax certificate on file. Keeps collections team happy.

- Withholding: we _cannot_ accept open-ended liability. Recommend language: "Customer is responsible for any taxes, duties, or withholdings imposed by Customer's jurisdiction; upon request Customer must provide official tax documentation (W-8/W-9 or local equivalent) to claim exemption or change withholding rates."

I flagged two small redlines in the attached draft (see comments in RED-OrderForm-draft-v2.pdf).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara@edgescale.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: RED draft: billing cadence, invoice entity options & tax evidence request

Hi Sara / Procurement — thanks again for the productive call last week. Attaching a revised order form (RED-OrderForm-draft-v2.pdf) that captures the commercial schedule we discussed plus the few gating items we need confirmed for legal and accounting sign-off. Summary of the asks below: 

1) Commit cadence: we’ve proposed three tranches (signature + 90 days + 180 days) with a year-end true-up. If EdgeScale prefers a single up-front payment, we can accept that but need it confirmed in writing along with PO details.

2) Invoice entity: please confirm the entity you want invoices addressed to (EdgeScale Global, Inc. or EdgeScale EU Ltd.). If you plan to change remit entity later, please confirm you will provide 30 days notice and the appropriate tax certificate (e.g., VAT registration or W-8).

3) Withholding and VAT: to avoid surprise deductions, please confirm whether EdgeScale will withhold at source in any jurisdiction. If so, please attach the supporting tax documentation so we can document the exemption/withholding in the order form appendix.

Attachments included: RED-OrderForm-draft-v2.pdf (our proposed text), sample tax evidence checklist.

Target next steps: if you can confirm items 1-3 and return a PO (or confirm single upfront payment and PO number) by COB Thu 16 Apr, legal will finalize redlines and we can route for signature. Also included link to DocuSign room for faster sign-off: https://docusign.com/rooms/ES-2026-0411

Thanks — looping Ben and Karthik for any follow-ups on finance/ops side.

Best,
Kimberly
From: Sara Lin <sara@edgescale.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@edgescale.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RED draft: billing cadence, invoice entity options & tax evidence request

Thanks Kimberly — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers and attachments: 

1) Commit cadence: EdgeScale is OK with the 3-tranche approach but prefers the second tranche to be time-based (90 days) rather than usage-triggered — they want predictability for internal forecasting. They will accept the year-end true-up.

2) Invoice entity: please bill to EdgeScale Global, Inc. for the first year. If a remit entity change is required later, we will provide 30 days notice and the VAT/W-8 as appropriate.

3) Withholding/VAT: EdgeScale confirms they do not anticipate withholding on payments from the US entity. Attached: EdgeScale-W8.pdf (tax form) and a sample PO: EdgeScale-PO-67891.pdf.

We reviewed Ben's comments; we can accept the 30-day notice for entity changes. Regarding the conditionality Ben suggested, EdgeScale prefers fixed dates to avoid complexity — any chance Redwood can accept fixed 90/180 day invoices without a usage floor?
